audience: A PC-literate Romanian 12th-grade student. Explain in clear English from foundations, not compressed certification jargon.
style: Original teaching, not copied Microsoft lesson text or leaked exam material.
Never use an em dash, its HTML entity or numeric entity.
Introduce each concept and acronym before relying on it. State what problem it solves, how it works, when to choose it, and what it does not do.
Use the existing fictional school application where helpful: school people, web application, private database, document archive and office.
Use concrete names, addresses and calculations with explicit assumptions. No real credentials, tenants or subscriptions.
Separate management-plane authorization, data-plane authorization, network reachability and application authentication.
Avoid filler, repetitive boilerplate, invented exam probabilities and unsupported guarantees.
moduleContract: Use AuthoredModuleSchema in src/domain/course.ts. New IDs are listed in curriculum.json; while the framework branch is pending, validate with an otherwise identical schema that extends only the id enum. No new module/lesson fields are needed for authors.
lessonRequirements: Use exactly the allocated lesson IDs and order. Four to twelve meaningful sections per lesson, normally at least 900 words of explanatory content; satisfy the curriculum's module minimum without padding.
Every lesson has a genuine worked example with action/why steps, a prediction with explained reveal, and an exam-context distinction.
Every lesson has three to five original scored checkpoints, normally four, with an explanation for every correct and incorrect option.
Use at least one explanatory diagram per module. Declared nodes must fit the existing 3 by 3 renderer.
Keep checkpoint answers unambiguous under stated assumptions. Include precise SKU, region or preview qualifications when necessary.
Required knowledge must be taught in the lesson, not outsourced to a linked document or optional Azure lab.
Include optional manual labs with prerequisites, potential charges, observable outcomes and narrow cleanup. Never execute Azure provisioning.
sourceRequirements: Ground claims in current first-party Microsoft documentation and use documentation search/fetch rather than memory alone.
Use the official code-sample search before adding ARM, Bicep, Azure CLI, PowerShell or KQL examples.
Read high-risk feature/SKU/limit prerequisites in full. Confirm whether a feature is GA, preview, retired or changed.
Module source URL and lesson IDs must match curriculum.json. Source entries identify the exact claims they support.
Source availability is not factual validation. Independently trace the worked reasoning and checkpoint keys.
If documentation conflicts or varies by deployment type, state the scope explicitly rather than invent certainty.

lessons.evidence: Explain how the cited sections teach the objective and what the learner can actually reason through or do.

rules: Cover each objective assigned to the domain exactly once at the objective-entry level.
Targets can include multiple lessons. Each referenced section/checkpoint must exist in the correct module/lesson.
Each objective needs at least one substantial worked application across its targets, not just a mention or glossary item.
At least one checkpoint per objective is preferred; explain an empty checkpoint list if the objective is assessed in a shared practical scenario.
Monitoring objective mo-06 can reference the existing networking Network Watcher module in addition to new monitoring lessons.

reviewApprovals: Authors do not approve their own work. The coordinator binds independently reviewed module digests in per-domain approval files after the review.
commitPolicy: Commit only owned source/coverage files in your child branch with a clear domain-sized message and the required Copilot coauthor trailer. Do not push main, create a pull request or deploy. The coordinator integrates, reviews, pushes and publishes.
